title: KV offload tier: measure whether LMCache is a cost, not just a hit rate
description: User's framing (2026-08-22): LMCache may well be the bottleneck - do not assume it helps. Layerwise transfer is the thing that makes it competitive and it may not work; without it the fetch serializes against compute. So the experiment must be able to conclude 'offload made it worse'. Four points per config, not one: (1) insert cost - does writing every block to host RAM slow the FIRST request, (2) GPU-warm TTFT - the ceiling, (3) evicted-then-fetched TTFT - the offload hit, which is the number that either beats or loses to recompute, (4) never-seen TTFT - full prefill, the floor. Plus a pure-overhead control: if a salted prefix that can never hit is slower with the tier attached, the tier costs even when idle. Arms: GPU-only / LMCache CPU tier / layerwise on-off if the knob exists. Do this on the local RTX 3070 with Qwen2.5-1.5B and --num-gpu-blocks-override to make eviction cheap - iterating on a rented H200 costs money for what is a config hunt. Context: on the H200 (2026-08-21) LMCache 0.5.3 initialised then hung 10min in local_cpu_backend with MAX_LOCAL_CPU_SIZE=600 and 'lmcache.c_ops compiled extension not found'. Reference numbers to beat: GPU-warm 0.157s vs recompute 2.319s at 54k tokens; KV is ~41.5KB/token so 54k tokens is ~2.2GB over PCIe.

title: Driver: run the H200 A/B through testbed/vast_run.sh
description: testbed/vast_run.sh does search (price ceiling enforced on the chosen offer) -> create -> poll (terminal statuses handled) -> seed snapshots -> bootstrap over ssh -> periodic pull -> verify -> destroy, and records the rented machine (GPU, host, dph_total, network, driver) into the run dir while it still exists. Validated only with --dry-run: no vastai CLI or API key on this box. First real use is the gpt-oss-120b prefix-cache A/B. Watch for: gpu_name value for H200 on vast (H200 vs H200_NVL/SXM), whether 'disk_space' and 'dph_total' are valid search fields (an invalid field is silently ignored - the ceiling guard covers it), and that the image's passive CMD keeps the instance in 'running'.

title: Run the prefix-cache A/B on a rented H200 with gpt-oss-120b
description: The axis the hosted endpoint cannot measure (no prefix cache: cached_tokens absent, TTFT flat across identical prefixes, verified 2026-08-08). Validated end to end on this box with Qwen2.5-1.5B: stable prefix warms 0.54s -> 0.024s TTFT with 2240/2258 tokens cached, salted control flat at 0.203s, caching-off flat at 0.216s. Remaining: model parity. gpt-oss-120b (MXFP4 ~63GB) needs 1xH200 141GB for KV headroom - the cache budget IS the independent variable, so H100 80GB risks confounding it. Two runs, same RUN_ID convention: PREFIX_CACHING=on and off, SCALES='1 10', 7-9 arms. Outputs must carry runmeta manifest, endpoint descriptor, serve flags, metrics.jsonl and raw episode samples. This is a NEW arm - it does not replace any published figure.

Also re-measure the rust w=8 server 15.3ms/call outlier. Run in both venvs: ~/.venvs/neo4j-pure and ~/.venvs/neo4j-rust, database finbenchl1.

title: Remove scripts package import collision with OpenAI Agents SDK
description: Discovered while failure-path testing AIsummit26-xom. scripts/__init__.py prepends scripts/agents to sys.path; importing scripts.benchmarks.bench_framework_context as a module can therefore resolve top-level agents to the repo's scripts/agents package rather than the installed OpenAI Agents SDK. Direct CLI execution is unaffected. Refactor legacy bootstrap paths and add an import regression test.

title: vLLM-Hook: which part of the ontology prefix does the model actually attend to
description: User confirmed this as a talk episode (2026-08-22). IBM vLLM-Hook (github.com/IBM/vLLM-Hook, checkout at ~/vllm-hook) has attention_tracker and token_highlighter plugins. The follow-on question to the prefix-cache result is exactly this: we pay to keep a 54k-token ontology prefix resident, so which of its sections does the model read when writing Cypher? If attention concentrates on a fraction, the engineering move is to shrink or reorder the prefix rather than to buy more KV. HARD CONSTRAINT: its requirement.txt pins vllm>=0.5,<=0.21 while every number in results/ is from 0.27.1 - it cannot share a server with the arms, and 0.21 lacks the V1 metrics (--kv-cache-metrics, prompt_tokens_details) the A/B depends on. So: separate diagnostic run on a pinned 0.21 environment, its own venv, and its attention figures must never be placed in the same chart as 0.27.1 latency numbers.

title: Seed SF100 to S3 instead of regenerating it on the GPU box
description: GENERATE_MISSING=1 is proven byte-identical for SF1 (counts and checksums match the committed manifest), so a fresh clone can regenerate SF1/SF10 cheaply. SF100 is 36MB of parquet and the slow generation; doing it on a metered GPU instance pays inference rates for a DuckDB job. Push it once from a CPU box, content-addressed by manifest sha, and let the instance pull. Blocked on the bucket.

title: Wire S3 checkpointing end to end (bucket still unnamed)
description: scripts/testbed/s3_ckpt.py is written and its content-addressing verified locally (sf1 -> sf1/8d317c0796145f34), but no bucket/region/profile has been named, so push-datasets / pull-datasets / watch / verify have never made a real round trip. Blocks the destroy gate being meaningful on a rented instance: without S3, results/runs/<id> exists only on the box and must be copied down by hand before destroy. Needs: bucket + region from the user, boto3 installed, one round trip proven for a dataset and a run dir, and the resume log's watch loop confirmed to keep a growing file in sync.
